output:

Spent the last 2 Saturdays redoing the electric on a buddy's shed. I've been doing this 26 years and I thought I'd seen it all. I had not seen it all.

Here's the inventory of what we pulled out of there, in no particular order:

1. The "power" to the shed was 3 orange extension cords daisy chained together. Out the basement window, across the yard, under the deck, into the shed. Every time somebody mowed the lawn it was a game of chance.

2. One of the splices between those cords was wrapped in duct tape. Not electrical tape. DUCT tape. Like he was fixing a hose.

3. A 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire. For anybody who doesn't do this, that means the wire is going to cook long before the breaker ever thinks about tripping. The breaker is supposed to protect the wire. This breaker was just there for moral support.

4. The outlet in the shed was hooked up with speaker wire. Speaker wire. I had to go stand outside for a minute.

5. The "GFCI" outlet was a regular outlet with a GFCI sticker stuck on it. I respect the confidence honestly.

6. The ceiling fan box was held up by one drywall screw. One. Hanging over the spot where you'd sit and have a beer.

7. Mouse nest inside a junction box. The mice were fine. Totally unbothered. Probably the safest ones in the shed because they had the sense to stay off the speaker wire.

And my favorite. When I opened the panel the wife was standing right there, and on the inside of the panel door in sharpie it says SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON

She goes "who's Ron?" like I'd know. Nobody knows who Ron is. Ron is gone. Ron's legacy lives on in that panel door.

And look, I'm not trashing Ron. Ron wasn't evil. Ron was cheap and a little proud, and that's most of the stuff I find in people's houses. Somebody didn't want to pay for it, figured how hard can it be, watched a video, and it worked. Fan spins, light comes on, so it must be right. Then it sits there for 10 years until it isn't.

What we did: trenched it 18 inches, ran 12/2 UF out to the shed, put in a 20 amp GFCI breaker, real box, real outlets, fan on a proper brace. Now it's done right and nothing smells like it's burning. I got paid in 2 pizzas and a case of Yuengling, which is the correct rate for family and friends.

Now the serious part, and I mean it.

Every single thing on that list is how houses burn down. Wrong size wire on the wrong breaker gets hot inside your walls where you can't see it or smell it until it's too late. Fake GFCI means the thing that's supposed to keep you from getting lit up in a wet shed doesn't do a thing. Duct tape splices sitting in the grass, come on.

So please. If you need something wired, call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy who watched a YouTube video. Not your nephew's friend who'll do it for cash this weekend. I know a licensed guy costs more up front. It's still cheaper than a fire, and way cheaper than somebody getting hurt. Get it permitted and get it inspected. That's how you know it was done right, and if it ever goes wrong, insurance doesn't get to look at you funny.

And if you open your panel and somebody's name is written on the door in sharpie, that's your sign to get it looked at.

Ron, wherever you are, we fixed it buddy. 🍕⚡

reasons: It reveals the private message’s detail that nothing smells like burning.
